blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Glenbrooke North lies between Sixth Avenue and Tenth Avenue, with Sixth Street on the west and McBride Boulevard on the east, per the City's Historical Neighbourhood Context Statement for Glenbrooke North.

The City spells the name Glenbrooke North; the board report spelling GlenBrooke North, with a capital B, is the same neighbourhood, north of Queen's Park around Glenbrook Ravine, Jamieson Court and Park Crescent.

Second Street and Fifth Street boulevards run north from Queen's Park into Glenbrooke North, and the filled Glenbrooke Creek bed cuts across the neighbourhood's northeast corner, per the City context statement.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here span the Edwardian-era fabric on Fifth Street south of Eighth Avenue to the 1950s subdivision character along Eighth Avenue and east of Fourth Street, per the City context statement.

Detached houses are freehold under the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series) in Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001; RS-1 sets a minimum site of 557.40 square metres with a floor space ratio of 0.5.
École Glenbrook Middle School at 701 Park Crescent and Herbert Spencer Elementary at 605 Second Street are the school buildings inside the house streets, not commercial anchors.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Official Community Plan designation for most Glenbrooke North house lots is Residential – Detached and Semi-Detached Housing (RD), whose stated intent is houses, secondary suites, laneway or carriage houses and duplexes.

The City's infill housing work expressly names Glenbrooke North among the low-density neighbourhoods whose Detached and Semi-Detached and Ground Oriented Infill designations cover houses, suites, laneway and carriage houses, small lots, duplexes and triplexes.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Terry Hughes Park, between Seventh and Eighth Avenues adjoining McBride Boulevard, was leased from the federal penitentiary site in 1956 — the green edge on this area's east side is former federal land, per the City context statement.
The BC Penitentiary Cemetery near 245 Francis Way, at the area's southeast edge, was established in 1913, used until 1968, and restored and unveiled by the City on August 29, 2018.
Glenbrook Ravine was reserved by Colonel Moody in 1859 as Queen's Ravine, and the City's park history calls it the first public park in the Colony of British Columbia.
The təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue, whose aquatic portion opened May 14, 2024, is the nearest major recreation centre, east of this area.
Cherry trees line the north end of the Second Street blocks by Queen's Park, a context-statement detail that marks the boulevard streets at this area's south edge.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: development and new projects

items.t: City-wide, the Official Community Plan was amended in 2026 for Transit Oriented Development extensions, Amendment Bylaw No. 8574, 2026 — Glenbrooke North has no SkyTrain station, so that amendment touches its edges, not its centre.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: Glenbrooke-specific utility fact: a single-family dwelling here pays the City's 2026 flat-rate utilities of $881.20 net for water and $1,364.21 net for sewer after the 5 percent discount, with the discounted amount requiring full payment by May 4, 2026; a house with a secondary suite pays a higher combined total.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: getting around

items.t: Route 109, New Westminster Station / Lougheed Station, runs via Richmond Street and Jamieson Court, turning around on Jamieson Court — the Glenbrook Ravine access street itself carries the bus loop.
Route 102, Victoria Hill, returns via Blackberry Drive, another ravine access street, then Francis Way and Memorial Drive; route 155 runs on Richmond Street along the area's east side.
No SkyTrain station is inside Glenbrooke North: the City lists five stations in New Westminster — 22nd Street, New Westminster, Columbia, Sapperton and Braid — and the closest depends on the address.
McBride Boulevard on the east edge and Eighth Avenue and Eighth Street carry driving traffic south to Downtown and the Pattullo Bridge approach and north to Sapperton.

blocks.text: Glenbrooke North Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check slope and ravine setbacks for any lot backing onto Glenbrook Ravine: the ravine is a steep, forested watercourse corridor in the City Green Zone, and the park page's staircases and trails describe grade, not a lot's buildable area.

Check flood status per address on the City Flood Susceptibility Map: the City states five of its twelve square kilometres lie within the provincial floodplain boundaries, covering Queensborough and sections of the mainland — Glenbrooke North's hill position must still be verified per lot.

Check the filled creek bed in the northeast corner: the City context statement records that Glenbrooke Creek's ravine was filled in 1914 for a combined sewer, so ground conditions there differ from the surrounding streets.

blocks.text: GlenBrooke North home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

25 houses sold in GlenBrooke North with a median price of $1,575,000 (the middle half sold between $1,300,000 and $1,890,000), taking a median of 23 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 24% sold above list. They had a median $603 per square foot, a median year built of 1945 and a median lot of 6,600 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in GlenBrooke North?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 12 houses listed in GlenBrooke North. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is GlenBrooke North a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in GlenBrooke North had a sales ratio of 33%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in GlenBrooke North from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 15 houses sold in GlenBrooke North over those 5 months, out of 75 in all of New Westminster.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in GlenBrooke North?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Glenbrooke North house?
faq.a: Check the exact address, because catchments split here. A School District No. 40 school locator run for a nearby address returned F.W. Howay Elementary, École Glenbrook Middle and New Westminster Secondary, while Herbert Spencer Elementary at 605 Second Street stands inside this neighbourhood and offers Early French Immersion as a program of choice.

faq.q: Is Glenbrooke North under Queen's Park heritage rules?
faq.a: No. Glenbrooke North has a Historic Neighbourhood Context Statement, which documents its history, but it is not a Heritage Conservation Area. The Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area, with its protection for existing buildings and design guidelines, adjoins it to the south and stops at that boundary.

faq.q: What is the ravine behind the Park Crescent houses?
faq.a: Glenbrook Ravine Park, 13.38 acres established in 1991, with access points on Jamieson Court, Blackberry Drive and Glenbrooke Drive, each with winding staircases and hard-packed trails, plus a pond, falls and bridge in its cultivated section. Lots backing onto it trade a park edge for a steep slope.

faq.q: Can I add a laneway house on an Eighth Avenue lot?
faq.a: On most lots, yes in principle. RS-1 zoning permits a detached accessory dwelling unit alongside the house and a secondary suite, and the lot sits in the Laneway and Carriage House Development Permit Area, so a development permit and the design guidelines apply before a building permit.

faq.q: What did houses in GlenBrooke North sell for?
faq.a: 25 houses sold in GlenBrooke North between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,575,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in GlenBrooke North?
faq.a: The median was 23 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 96.9% of the last list price (24% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
